title: Incorrect/Inconsistent behavior of Normals w/ Negative Scaling between MultiMeshRendering and SingleMeshRendering.
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible on Godot 4.4.1 and 4.5 Beta 3 ### System information Godot v4.5.beta3.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 SUPER (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7602) - AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 63.62 GiB memory ### Issue description The handling for negative scale values in transforms is inconsistent between rendering single instances in the Rendering Server and rendering Multimeshes. In specific, it seems to be incorrect for MultiMesh Rendering. The following list of test cases represent the inconsistencies/errors: 1. **Correct Normals:** - MeshInstance nodes with negatively scaled transforms. 2. **Correct Normals:** - Singular meshes rendered via RenderingServer.instance_create(). 3. **Correct Normals:** - MultiMeshInstance *Nodes* which are rendering a MultiMesh *Resource* instance with a positively scaled transform, but a negatively scaled transform on the *Node* itself. 4. **Incorrect Normals:** - MultiMeshInstance *Nodes* which are rendering a MultiMesh *Resource* instance with a negatively scaled transform. 5. **Incorrect Normals:** - MultiMeshes rendered via RenderingServer.instance_create() which have negatively scaled transforms ( set via RenderingServer.multimesh_set_buffer() ). This bug seems to persist across Forward+, Mobile, and Compatibility rendering modes, and on both Vulkan and D3D12 for Windows, though I'm not 100% sure I did the D3D12 toggle correctly, so someone may want to re-check that. ### Steps to reproduce See Minimum Reproduction Project 1. Play project 2. Observe the labels atop the various methods of rendering the same flipped mesh. Note that some methods have correctly flipped normals (facing the camera, look normal), while others have incorrect, broken normals. In specific, all formats where a multimesh is given a transform containing an odd number of negative scale values. Or manual reproduction steps: 1. Create a single Mesh Rendering Instance via the Rendering Server. 2. Provide it with a Transform scaled with exactly one axis /an uneven number of axes negative. (Ex. (-1, 1, 1)) 3. Observe that the singularly rendered mesh renders correctly. 4. Create a MultiMeshInstance via the Rendering Server. 5. Use the same Transform in the Multimesh Instance buffer. 6. Observe that the MultiMesh rendered mesh renders incorrectly. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [MultimeshRenderingBugs MRP2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21338410/MultimeshRenderingBugs.MRP2.zip)
